definition.description: The 'Axis of Awesome' progression — used in countless pop hits
definition.name: Pop: I-V-vi-IV

definition.description: The foundational three-chord rock/blues progression
definition.name: Classic: I-IV-V

definition.description: The quintessential 12-bar blues form
definition.name: Blues: 12-Bar (I-IV-V)

definition.description: The most important progression in jazz; appears in virtually every standard
definition.name: Jazz: ii-V-I

definition.description: The '50s progression' or 'doo-wop progression'
definition.name: 50s: I-vi-IV-V

definition.description: Based on Pachelbel's Canon — descending fifth circular motion
definition.name: Classical: Pachelbel (I-V-vi-iii-IV-I-IV-V)

definition.description: Same chords as I-V-vi-IV starting on vi — more melancholic, yearning quality
definition.name: Pop: vi-IV-I-V

definition.description: Uses the flattened 7th degree from mixolydian mode — quintessential rock sound
definition.name: Rock: I-bVII-IV

definition.description: Simplest common progression — creates an open, unresolved vamp
definition.name: Folk: I-IV

definition.description: Minor-key equivalent of vi-IV-I-V — extremely common in modern pop and EDM
definition.name: Pop: i-VI-III-VII

definition.description: All-natural-minor diatonic chords — the most common minor-key four-chord loop
definition.name: Pop: i-bVI-bIII-bVII

definition.description: Fusion of Pachelbel's Canon with rock — uses harmonic minor raised 7th
definition.name: Rock: V-i-VI-IV (Canon Rock)

definition.description: Borrowing iv from parallel minor — creates emotional, bittersweet color
definition.name: Modal Interchange: I-iv

definition.description: Chromatic mediant I→III plus modal interchange IV→iv — iconic Radiohead sound
definition.name: Modal Interchange: I-III-IV-iv (Creep)

definition.description: Roots a major third apart — creates a dramatic, cinematic quality
definition.name: Chromatic Mediant: I-bIII
notable_songs: Where the Streets Have No Name

definition.description: bVI borrowed from parallel minor — creates a broad, heroic, expansive quality
definition.name: Chromatic Mediant: I-bVI

definition.description: Roots a major third apart, both major — bright, unexpected harmonic lift
definition.name: Chromatic Mediant: I-III

definition.description: The Neapolitan chord (bII major) — dramatic pre-dominant function; related to tritone substitution
definition.name: Classical: Neapolitan (i-bII-V-i)

definition.description: Chromatic descending bass line — sophisticated and emotive; common in jazz ballads
definition.name: Chromatic: Descending Bass (I-i7-IV-iv6-I)

definition.description: Chromatic descending bass — the 'James Bond' chord progression; cinematic and mysterious
definition.name: Chromatic: Line Cliche (i-bVII-bVI-V)

definition.description: Baroque descending bass line with passing diminished chord — foundational in classical music
definition.name: Classical: Omnipotent (I-VII-iv-iv°-III-II-I)

definition.description: Ascending stepwise motion through diatonic chords — gentle, building, optimistic
definition.name: Pop: Ascending (I-ii-iii-IV)

definition.description: Stepwise descent from I to bVI with return through bVII — dramatic harmonic gesture
definition.name: Rock: Chromatic Walkdown (I-bVII-VI-bVII-I)

definition.description: The most famous flamenco progression — descending bass from i to V; the raised 7th provides Spanish tension
definition.name: Flamenco: Andalusian Cadence (i-bVII-bVI-V)

definition.description: Phrygian dominant scale (5th mode of harmonic minor) — the tonic is major and the bII creates the characteristic flamenco bite
definition.name: Flamenco: Phrygian Dominant (I-bII-bIII-bII)

definition.description: Uses raised 7th (V instead of bVII) from harmonic minor for stronger dominant-tonal resolution
definition.name: Harmonic Minor: i-iv-V

definition.description: Based on the double harmonic scale with augmented 2nd intervals — the I-bII is the signature sound
definition.name: Exotic: Byzantine / Double Harmonic (I-bII-I)
notable_songs: Greek and Middle Eastern traditional music

definition.description: Hungarian minor scale (harmonic minor with raised 4th) — distinctive Eastern European / gypsy flavor
definition.genre: Hungarian, Eastern European, klezmer, gypsy jazz
definition.name: Exotic: Hungarian Minor (i-bII-iv)

definition.description: Based on hirajoshi pentatonic scale — distinctly Japanese harmonic colors; bII and bVI give Asian-influenced sound
definition.name: World: Japanese / Hirajoshi (I-bII-V-bVI)

definition.description: The Hijaz mode/makam (phrygian dominant) — the tonic is major and the augmented 2nd between bII and bIII is the hallmark of Middle Eastern music
definition.name: World: Hijaz / Makam (I-bII-bIII-iv)

definition.description: 'Freygish' = Yiddish for phrygian dominant — the tonic is major and the I-bII-III movement is the core of klezmer harmony
definition.name: World: Klezmer / Freygish (I-bII-III-VII)

definition.description: The raised 6th in dorian gives a brighter quality than natural minor — common in modal jazz
definition.name: Modal: Dorian Vamp (i-IV)

definition.description: Combines dorian brightness with aeolian — the IV chord is the key dorian characteristic
definition.name: Modal: Dorian-Aeolian (i-bVII-IV)

definition.description: The II chord (major, not diminished) comes from the lydian raised 4th — floating, ethereal, dreamlike
definition.name: Modal: Lydian (I-II)

definition.description: Based on the whole tone scale — augmented chords create a floating, ambiguous, otherworldly quality
definition.name: Modal: Whole Tone (I-II-III)

definition.description: Combines mixolydian bVII with modal interchange bVI — rock anthem quality with dramatic lift
definition.name: Modal: Mixolydian bVI (I-bVII-bVI-bVII)

definition.description: The simplest phrygian vamp — the bII major chord creates the characteristic dark, tense phrygian sound
definition.name: Modal: Phrygian (i-bII-i)

definition.description: Adds the III chord to the phrygian vamp — common in Spanish guitar music
definition.name: Modal: Spanish Phrygian (i-bII-III)

definition.description: All dominant 7th chords — the defining blues characteristic (dominant 7th on I doesn't fit diatonic major)
definition.name: Blues: Dominant 7th (I7-IV7-V7)

definition.description: Minor-key blues — the V7 uses the harmonic minor raised 7th for stronger resolution
definition.name: Blues: Minor Blues (i7-iv7-V7)
notable_songs: As The Years Go Passing By

definition.description: The A section of rhythm changes — one of the two most important progressions in jazz (with blues)
definition.name: Jazz: Rhythm Changes A (I-vi-ii-V)

definition.description: The B section (bridge) of rhythm changes — circle of fifths through secondary dominants
definition.name: Jazz: Rhythm Changes B (III7-VI7-II7-V7)

definition.description: Root movement by major thirds — three key centers an augmented triad apart; Coltrane's harmonic innovation
definition.name: Jazz: Coltrane Changes (Giant Steps)

definition.description: Inserts a ii-V-I a major third away before resolving — creates rapid harmonic motion through distant keys
definition.name: Jazz: Coltrane Sub (ii-V-I with major third substitution)

definition.description: Resolves to I via the 'back door' using iv and its dominant bVII7 — very common in modern jazz
definition.name: Jazz: Backdoor (iv-bVII7-I)

definition.description: The standard jazz turnaround — leads back to the top of the form; supports many substitutions
definition.name: Jazz: Turnaround (I-vi-ii-V)
notable_songs: end of nearly every jazz standard

definition.description: The minor key version of ii-V-I — ii is half-diminished (m7b5), V7 uses harmonic minor raised 7th
definition.name: Jazz: Minor ii-V-i

definition.description: Replaces V7 with bII7 — shares the same tritone, creating a chromatic bass descent; essential jazz substitution
definition.name: Jazz: Tritone Substitution (ii-bII7-I)

definition.description: Uses a secondary dominant (V/ii) to approach ii chromatically — creates forward harmonic motion
definition.name: Jazz: Secondary Dominant (I-V/ii-ii-V-I)

definition.description: Charlie Parker's reharmonization of the 12-bar blues with ii-V chains and substitutions
definition.name: Jazz: Bird Blues

definition.description: Modal jazz uses very few chords — often just a vamp, allowing extended improvisation on a single mode
definition.name: Jazz: Modal Vamp (i-iv)

definition.description: Extended circle-of-fifths chain — each chord resolves down a fifth to the next; smooth continuous motion
definition.name: Jazz: Extended Chain (iii-vi-ii-V-I)
notable_songs: many jazz standards, especially intros and turnarounds

definition.description: The IV to iv movement — one of the most expressive modal interchange devices; also called 'minor plagal cadence'
definition.name: Jazz: IV-iv-I (Minor Subdominant)

definition.description: The 'Amen' cadence — less final than V-I but with a warm, resolved quality
definition.name: Classical: Plagal (IV-I)

definition.description: The V resolves deceptively to vi instead of I — creates surprise and extends the phrase
definition.name: Classical: Deceptive (V-vi)

definition.description: The minor subdominant resolving to major tonic — bittersweet, nostalgic quality; very expressive modal interchange
definition.name: Classical: Minor Plagal (iv-I)

definition.description: The jazz blues adds ii-V chains and turnarounds to the basic blues form
definition.name: Jazz: Jazz Blues

definition.description: Brazilian jazz typically uses ii-V-I with extended chord voicings (9ths, 11ths, 13ths)
definition.name: Jazz: Bossa Nova (ii-V-I)

definition.description: The most important song form in jazz besides blues — 32 bars in AABA structure
definition.name: Jazz: AABA Form

output.label: Jazz: Coltrane Sub (ii-V-I with major third substitution)
